- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 15–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model underestimates; increase forecast by 15–30% for low sentiment periods.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment — cap forecast growth after 2–3 consecutive high sentiment days.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent mean reversion bias: if 18-day history is stable, forecast should not deviate > ±1.5x from recent 7-day average.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day avg), model often overshoots by 20–50% — apply decay factor of 0.85 to subsequent forecast values.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– cycles (e.g., +0.33, -0.33, +0.33), model tends to misalign with true trend — align forecast to sentiment polarity average over 3–5 days.
